owner_decision: On 2026-11-22 the owner decided that what is needed is researched online and the twin works on declared assumptions; the professional review of these assumptions will be by Wolfe Classics, the seller of the scan. Nobody was contacted for this record.
rule: A published value is a declared hypothesis with its source, never a measurement of the specimen. A value with no source stays null with a named blocker. A fitted value is a number fitted on the scan, whose unit is the owner's instruction (1 OBJ unit = 1 mm); its check against published values is params/scale-check.json.
claims: This record names the identity the twin assumes from now on and the evidence for and against it. It identifies nothing by resemblance: no published document names this specimen's engine, bore, program, part number or casting mark. The assumed identity is H16 and H17 in hypotheses.json.

scan.unit: 1 OBJ unit = 1 mm by owner instruction; checked against published values in params/scale-check.json, never measured

candidates.description: Xtreme casting of the 2.0 - 2.9 liter program, prepared for the 2.85 L 935 (bore at most 92.8 mm), twin plug
evidence_for: the seller says the head was made for a 935 race car (pv-listing-text) and the seller's private statement names the maker (pv-maker-statement)
Porsche gives the 935 a 2.85 L engine (pv-935-displacement-porsche), inside this program's range
under the 1 mm unit the chamber shoulder (92.80 mm) equals the 92.8 mm published bore and the class-limit bore (f-chamber-shoulder)
two plug bores, as in the 935's twin ignition (f-plug-count)
evidence_against: published bores of the 2.85 L 935 disagree (92.0, 92.4, 92.8 mm)
valve_y_plus's 43.0 mm mid-band seat is larger than this program's largest exhaust valve, 41.5 mm (f-seats-throats; weak, since where a valve seats on the cone is not published)
the 935 also raced with 3.0 to 3.3 L engines (pv-935-other-capacities)

candidates.description: Xtreme casting of the 3.0 - 3.5 liter program (bores of 95 mm and more), twin plug, for a 3.0 to 3.3 L 935-type engine
evidence_for: the 935 raced with 3.0 to 3.3 L engines (pv-935-other-capacities)
valve_y_plus's seat and throat sizes sit closer to this program's exhaust valves (f-seats-throats)
this program lists a 930 intake flange option (pv-xtreme-3.0-3.5-flange)
evidence_against: under the 1 mm unit the chamber edge (92.80 mm) is 2.2 mm smaller than a 95 mm bore: either the head overhangs the bore, which no source describes, or the scale is at least 1.024, while the guide-bore check points the other way (scale-check.json)
candidates.verdict: kept open; the chamber volume or the maker's statement would separate A and B

candidates.description: period Porsche 935 head (factory casting) or a modified production 930 head
evidence_for: the listing says the head was made specifically for a 935 (pv-listing-text)
evidence_against: the seller's statement names an aftermarket maker and a casting (pv-maker-statement)
the fitted guide bore (8.51 mm) is smaller than the production 9 mm stem (pv-964t-stem), so the head does not take the production valve under the 1 mm unit
the production 930 head has one plug per cylinder (pv-930-plugs-per-cylinder); the scan has two

candidates.description: Xtreme casting of a 3.6 - 4.0 liter program
evidence_for: the maker publishes these programs with the same 8 mm stems and 12 or 14 mm plugs (pv-xtreme-stems, pv-xtreme-plugs)
evidence_against: the seller ties the head to a 935 race car (pv-listing-text); the encyclopedia's summary gives the 935 engines of 2.8 to 3.3 L (pv-935-other-capacities)
if the chamber edge is the bore, a bore of 100 mm or more against the 92.80 mm chamber edge needs a scale of 1.078 or more, above the plug check's upper bound of 1.053 (scale-check.json)

questions_for_reviewer.question: Is the scanned head an Xtreme Cylinder Heads casting, cast then machined, and of which program and pattern revision? Is there a part number, serial or engraved logo on it, and where?
Which engine was it made for: displacement, bore and stroke, engine type, single or twin turbo? Is it a 935 replica build or a period configuration?
What bore is the chamber machined for, and is the chamber edge diameter equal to the bore? What are the register (cylinder spigot recess) diameter and depth, and is a fire ring fitted?
questions_for_reviewer.settles: H17, the conditional check of scale-check.json, the barrel of H13

questions_for_reviewer.question: What is the chamber volume as cc'd, with valves and plugs in, and to which face?
Which spark plugs: thread, pitch and reach (12 or 14 mm), and the same in both bores?
questions_for_reviewer.settles: H16 and the primary check of scale-check.json

questions_for_reviewer.question: Which flange side is the inlet? What are the valve head and stem diameters, the finished guide bore and guide material, and the seat insert materials and angles?
questions_for_reviewer.settles: H09, H05, the guide-bore discrepancy of scale-check.json

questions_for_reviewer.question: Was the head finish-machined when it was scanned (guides reamed, seats cut, studs fitted)? The scan's guide bore reads 8.51 mm against 8 mm stems.
How many head studs, of which thread, on which spacing; which thread for the cam-housing studs?
Which scanner took the scan (Creaform Handyscan 700 or Einstar Vega), was it calibrated at the time, was spray used, and is the OBJ in millimetres with no scaling or registration applied?
questions_for_reviewer.settles: #693: whether 1 OBJ unit = 1 mm is the scanner's own unit

questions_for_reviewer.question: What is the alloy, heat treatment and HIP state of this casting?
Under what licence may the project reuse the scan and any figure given in reply?
